steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Blue notes (flattened 3rd, 5th and 7th of the major scale) create the characteristic blues sound — they fall between the notes of the Western scale. | Key Fact: 12-bar blues follows a I-IV-V chord progression over three four-bar phrases: the AAB lyric structure mirrors this harmonic pattern. | Key Fact: Call and response between vocalist and guitar/harp creates dialogue — a fundamental feature inherited from African musical traditions. | Key Fact: Shuffle rhythm (long-short subdivision of the beat) gives blues its distinctive swing feel — it is notated in 12/8 or with triplets in 4/4.
